clinician.trajectory_summary: A young man in his 20s presented with fever, back pain, chills, headache, vomiting, and a painless rash on the right occipital region. He had a history of atopic dermatitis and lumbar disk hernia. Initial neurological examination showed no meningeal signs. CSF analysis revealed clear and colorless fluid with primarily mononuclear leukocytes, a glucose level of 28 mg/dL, and negative Gram stain, bacterial cultures, and serum HIV. HSV PCR on CSF was negative. VZV PCR on residual CSF detected VZV DNA at 11×10^6 copies/mL, confirming viral meningitis caused by VZV. The patient was admitted and treated with intravenous acyclovir and ampicillin, with ampicillin discontinued after negative cultures. A dermatologist diagnosed herpes zoster based on the rash's nature, distribution, and associated pain. Ten days later, the rash was crusted.
